idiom_name: ViewModel exposing MutableStateFlow or mutableStateOf consumed by Compose
implementation_notes: Android's architecture guidance names the output APIs directly: mutableStateOf for simple state (Compose recomposes only the scopes that read the changed state) and MutableStateFlow exposed as a read-only StateFlow for pipelines and tests, with the ViewModel holding the state across configuration changes. Events are the inputs and state is the output - 'state is; events happen' - so the view-model exposes a UI state type plus functions that transform it, and composables render it declaratively. Keep the state object immutable (data class + copy) when using StateFlow so equality-based conflation works.
pitfalls: A StateFlow is not a Compose State: collecting it without collectAsStateWithLifecycle ignores lifecycle and keeps collecting in the background.
MutableStateFlow conflates equal values by design; mutable fields or missing equality in the state class silently drop updates.
Starting coroutines in composition or collecting flows with the wrong launcher restarts work on every recomposition and leaks scopes.
The ViewModel survives configuration changes but not process death: state that must survive both belongs in SavedStateHandle.

variants.name: ViewModel + LiveData with XML layouts (view binding)
variants.idiom_name: ViewModel + MutableLiveData observed by XML-based Activities/Fragments
variants.implementation_notes: The pre-Compose route binds XML layouts to a ViewModel: MutableLiveData fields are observed with observe(viewLifecycleOwner) { ... }, view binding replaces findViewById, and LiveData's lifecycle awareness does the unsubscribing automatically. Use it when maintaining an XML-based UI; new screens should default to Compose and StateFlow, which give typed state and explicit recomposition scoping.
pitfalls: value must be set on the main thread (postValue from background); mixing them up crashes or reorders updates.
LiveData fires the last value when an observer becomes active again, so observer callbacks must be idempotent.
A ViewModel must not hold Activity/View/Context references; use the application context or ApplicationViewModel when one is genuinely needed.
Many independent LiveData fields make composite states partially updated between observers - prefer one immutable UI state object.
